about:
D-124 addendum (2026-10-09): edge time per driver pin for the reference-plane detour budget of tools/si_planes.py (tools/net_drivers.py reads this file). A net's edge is the shortest edge of its drivers, found in the schematic netlist. Roles: input (not a driver), push_pull (edge = min(tr, tf)), open_drain (open drain or open collector with a pull-up: edge = tf, the driver's fall; the RC rise is slower), opto (phototransistor output: min(tr, tf)), unknown (no published edge time: the net fails as 'unknown driver'). Statistic: the smallest value the document publishes (min, else typ, else max: then noted 'max only'). Each value: document, table, page, URL, [P] primary source read. Never a default: a part or pin with no rule is unknown.
D124c: IBIS drivers use load-dependent C*0.8*swing/I_avg from the Pulldown/Pullup static V-I tables over 10-90% of the swing, rather than the Ramp resistive fixture. Load is routed trace capacitance, sourced receiver capacitance and driver C_comp MIN; downstream series estimates omit upstream driver capacitance and may apply a 0.95*R current limit. All available corners and possible supply variants remain attributable; missing corners never inherit typical values. Open-drain fall uses the actual pull-up rail. Numeric V-I and C*dV/I estimates remain conditional screening values, never qualified fastest board-edge bounds; missing loads, model/load/PVT, transient/package and current/capacitance applicability are reported separately.

pins.source: ST TL072 datasheet (C6961), Dynamic electrical characteristics p. 5: tr rise time 0.1 us typ (small signal, unity gain); SR 16 V/us typ (8 min). Derivation: the small-signal step response of a linear amplifier has one shape for both polarities, so tf = tr; a large step is slew limited and slower (dV / SR). An op-amp output has no fixed swing, so the bound C*dV/I does not apply. TI and ST publish no IBIS model for the TL072 (TI product page, 2026-10-09). hardware-design/registry/datasheets/TL072CDT_C6961.pdf [P]
